findings.explanation: In no_sections mode, parsed.imports[section] raises KeyError for chained forced_separate sections with no entry in parsed.imports, and dict.update() silently overwrites same-module entries merged from different sections, losing imports/aliases.
findings.suggested_fix: Use parsed.imports.get(section, empty template) and merge per-import members instead of replacing whole module entries.

findings.explanation: pending_lines_before from a previous empty section forces blank lines before a section listed in config.no_lines_before, violating that section's explicit no-lines-before setting.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate on the current section: if not no_lines_before: output += [''] * config.lines_between_sections.

findings.explanation: Headings and footers share the single seen_headings set, so a footer equal to an earlier heading (or a later heading equal to an earlier footer) is incorrectly suppressed when dedup_headings is enabled.
findings.suggested_fix: Track seen headings and seen footers in separate sets.

findings.explanation: Duplicate heading/footer detection only checks the first/last line of lines_without_imports, so an existing heading/footer adjacent to imports elsewhere in the file is duplicated in the output.
findings.suggested_fix: Check against the lines adjacent to the import block (or all lines) rather than only lines_without_imports[0:1] / [-1:].

findings.explanation: Sections routed to parsed.place_imports are only emitted if their placement marker line appears verbatim in formatted_output; if the marker is absent (or the line text differs), those imports are silently dropped from the returned output.
findings.suggested_fix: After the loop, emit any place_imports sections whose placement was never matched (or raise/warn), instead of discarding them.

findings.explanation: Early return when import_index==-1 skips formatting_function, place_imports handling and string conversion performed on normal path.
findings.suggested_fix: Run shared post-processing or document that no imports means no formatting/placement.

findings.explanation: Merging sections assumes every section in itertools.chain exists in parsed.imports; forced_separate entries missing from parsed.imports raise KeyError.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard with `if section in parsed.imports` or use `.get()` with empty dicts.

findings.explanation: Function mutates input parsed object (adds no_sections entry, updates it, overwrites place_imports), so re-calling with same parsed double-merges and is not idempotent.
findings.suggested_fix: Work on deep copy of parsed.imports / place_imports instead of mutating parsed.

findings.explanation: Placed sections `continue` before headings, footers, separate_packages and spacing logic, so they lose that processing.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply headings/footers/separation before storing into place_imports.

findings.explanation: Heading duplicate check looks at parsed.lines_without_imports[0:1] instead of current output, causing duplicate headings on re-run or missed suppression.
findings.suggested_fix: Check `section_output`/`output` for existing comment before inserting.

findings.explanation: Footer check looks at parsed.lines_without_imports[-1:] instead of section output, and footers share seen_headings set with headings causing cross-suppression.
findings.suggested_fix: Check section_output for footer and use separate seen set for footers.

findings.explanation: Empty-section pending logic uses `or`: a pending separator is added even when current section is in no_lines_before, violating no_lines_before.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `if not no_lines_before and (pending_lines_before or True)` correctly e.g. `if not no_lines_before:` with pending only to force, or `pending and not no_lines_before`.

findings.explanation: Stripping with .strip()=='' treats form-feed-only lines as blank and discards \f characters that are preserved elsewhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Test `line.strip().strip('\f')==''` or preserve form feeds when trimming.

findings.explanation: .splitlines() drops trailing newline, normalizes all unicode line breaks and loses \r\n vs \n distinction.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `.split(parsed.line_separator)` or `splitlines(keepends=False)` handling preserving separator.

findings.explanation: When import_index >= original_line_count (imports at EOF) output_at falls back to 0, inserting imports at file start instead of at end.
findings.suggested_fix: Clamp to len(formatted_output), e.g. `output_at = min(parsed.import_index, len(formatted_output))`.

findings.explanation: lines_before_imports are prepended at index 0 instead of at output_at, so imports after docstring/code get padding at file top.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert at output_at: `formatted_output[output_at:output_at]=...` and adjust output_at/imports_tail.

findings.explanation: in_quote is reset to '' on every line, so multiline triple-quoted strings are never tracked across tail lines and next_construct is misidentified.
findings.suggested_fix: Carry in_quote across iterations: initialize before loop and update each iteration.

findings.explanation: next_construct.lstrip('\f') does not strip spaces/tabs, so indented STATEMENT_DECLARATIONS fail to trigger 2 lines_after_imports.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `next_construct.lstrip().lstrip('\f')` or strip whitespace.

findings.explanation: Condition `index <= lines_after_imports` is off-by-one and indexes past blank_lines, e.g. lines_after=1 index 1 or lines_after=0 index 0 raises IndexError.
findings.suggested_fix: Change to `if index < lines_after_imports:`.

findings.explanation: Placement lookup by line content duplicates placed imports for duplicate marker lines and raises KeyError if placed section was empty and never stored.
findings.suggested_fix: Track placements by index, ensure default empty list for missing place_imports entries.

findings.explanation: blank_lines has lines_after_imports entries (valid indices 0..lines_after_imports-1), but index == lines_after_imports is allowed by '<=' and blank_lines[index] raises IndexError when there are more trailing blank lines than lines_after_imports.
findings.suggested_fix: Use 'if index < lines_after_imports:' so excess form feeds fall into overflow_form_feeds.

findings.explanation: pending_lines_before accumulated from a previous empty section overrides the current section's no_lines_before entry, so blank lines are inserted before a section explicitly configured to have none.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate on the current section: 'if not no_lines_before and (pending_lines_before or output):' / only add separators when not no_lines_before.

findings.explanation: lines_before_imports blank lines are inserted at formatted_output[:0] (very top of file) rather than immediately before the imports at output_at, so files with a shebang/docstring/comments before imports get blank lines in the wrong place (breaking shebang recognition).
findings.suggested_fix: Insert at output_at: 'formatted_output[output_at:output_at] = [...]' and advance imports_tail accordingly.

findings.explanation: If parsed.import_index >= parsed.original_line_count (imports were at end of file), output_at stays 0 and the sorted imports are inserted at the top of the file instead of at the end.
findings.suggested_fix: Clamp to the end of lines_without_imports, e.g. output_at = min(parsed.import_index, len(formatted_output)).

findings.explanation: Headings and footers share seen_headings, so a footer whose text equals an earlier heading (or vice versa) is incorrectly suppressed when dedup_headings is enabled, even though they are distinct markers.
findings.suggested_fix: Use separate seen_headings and seen_footers sets.

findings.explanation: In no_sections mode, dict.update() overwrites an entry when the same module appears in multiple original sections (e.g. straight and lazy variants handled per-key), discarding imports recorded under the earlier section instead of merging them.
findings.suggested_fix: Merge per-module values (union/extend the stored import collections) rather than plain dict.update().

findings.explanation: Existing heading is only checked against the first line of the file and existing footer only against the last line; when imports are not at the file boundary an already-present heading/footer elsewhere is not detected and is duplicated.
findings.suggested_fix: Check membership against all of parsed.lines_without_imports (or the lines adjacent to the import block).

findings.explanation: Placement is triggered by raw line-text membership, so any repeated identical line in the file (not just the placement marker occurrence) re-extends the placed imports, duplicating them; an empty placed list also still appends a spurious blank line.
findings.suggested_fix: Track placement marker positions by index from parsing and insert once per marker, skipping empty placements.

findings.explanation: splitlines() splits on \f, \v, \x1c-\x1e, \x85 and unicode line boundaries in addition to the configured separator, corrupting any such characters in the formatting function's output and discarding the trailing empty line.
findings.suggested_fix: Split only on the separator: .split(parsed.line_separator).

findings.explanation: if not notes treats an existing empty list as missing and replaces it with a new list, losing object identity.
findings.suggested_fix: if notes is None: notes = []

findings.explanation: if not indexes treats an existing empty dict as missing and rebuilds it every time; stale state can desync from notes.
findings.suggested_fix: if indexes is None: indexes = {...}

findings.explanation: Membership is tested on notes list instead of indexes dict, O(n) and can diverge from indexes if env was pre-populated.
findings.suggested_fix: if key not in indexes: notes.append(key); indexes[key] = len(notes)-1

findings.explanation: footnote_ref token stores only normalized key as raw and index in attrs, losing original text and key needed to resolve the definition.
findings.suggested_fix: {"type":"footnote_ref", "raw": m.group(0), "attrs": {"key": key, "index": indexes[key]+1}}

findings.explanation: indexes is trusted whenever it is non-empty, even when notes was created as a new empty list because env['footnotes'] was missing or reset. A stale indexes entry is then overwritten with len(notes)-1, changing numbering for previously emitted refs and causing other stale entries to point outside or collide within notes.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep one source of truth or validate the cache: if notes was reset/missing, rebuild indexes from notes (indexes = {k:i for i,k in enumerate(notes)}) instead of reusing a non-empty cached dict.

findings.explanation: Membership is tested against notes but the token index is read from indexes. If key is already in notes (e.g. pre-seeded or appended by another footnote stage) but indexes was already created and does not contain key, line 16 raises KeyError instead of emitting the reference.
findings.suggested_fix: Test and fill the same mapping used for lookup, e.g. if key not in indexes: indexes[key]=len(notes); notes.append(key) only if key not in notes, or rebuild indexes when len(indexes)!=len(notes).

findings.explanation: The new env['footnote_indexes'] cache is introduced without invalidation tied to env['footnotes']; existing callers/plugins that reset only 'footnotes' between renders on a reused env keep the old indexes, so a later document inherits wrong footnote numbering and references to notes that no longer exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive indexes from footnotes on each parse or clear/rebuild footnote_indexes whenever footnotes is initialized/reset; do not let the cache outlive the footnotes list it describes.

findings.explanation: Condition is inverted: it discards existing footnotes when notes is truthy and leaves notes as None on first use.
findings.suggested_fix: if notes is None: notes = []

findings.explanation: When env has no footnotes, notes stays None so enumerate(notes) raises TypeError and notes.append raises AttributeError.
findings.suggested_fix: Initialize notes to [] before enumerate/append and always store it with state.env["footnotes"] = notes

findings.explanation: The guard is inverted: when no footnotes list exists yet, notes stays None, so enumerate(notes) on line 10 (or notes.append on line 13 if indexes already exists) raises TypeError/AttributeError on the first footnote reference.
findings.suggested_fix: Change line 6 to 'if not notes: notes = []' so a missing list is initialized.

findings.category: inverted condition / data loss and wrong index
findings.explanation: When a footnotes list already exists, it is discarded and replaced with [], so adding a subsequent distinct footnote overwrites state.env['footnotes'], loses earlier footnotes, and assigns the new key index 0 (rendered as 1), colliding with the first footnote.
findings.suggested_fix: Only initialize when missing: 'notes = state.env.get("footnotes"); if not notes: notes = []' and otherwise append to the existing list.

findings.explanation: After append, the new key is at last position len(notes)-1, not len(notes)-2. First footnote gets index -1 and every footnote is shifted, so attrs index is 0-based/wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: indexes[key] = len(notes) - 1

findings.explanation: if not notes treats empty list same as missing, discarding the list object from env and breaking aliasing. Should distinguish None from [].
findings.suggested_fix: if notes is None: notes = []; state.env["footnotes"] = notes

findings.explanation: if not indexes is true for empty dict, causing rebuild on every reference until first unique footnote and conflating missing with empty. Should check for None.
findings.suggested_fix: if indexes is None: indexes = {...}; state.env["footnote_indexes"] = indexes

findings.explanation: Newly created notes list is only stored in state.env inside if key not in indexes, so if notes was None but key was already indexed the env is never updated and state is lost.
findings.suggested_fix: Assign state.env["footnotes"] = notes immediately after creating it, unconditionally.

findings.explanation: After appending, the new footnote is at position len(notes)-1, but the code stores len(notes)-2. The first footnote therefore gets index -1 and token index 0, and every newly added footnote collides with the previous footnote's index.
findings.suggested_fix: Use indexes[key] = len(notes) - 1 after appending.

findings.explanation: When footnotes is missing or empty, a new detached list is created, but an existing non-empty footnote_indexes is retained. If the key is in that stale index map, the key is never appended to the new list and state.env['footnotes'] is never updated, yet a footnote_ref token referencing a non-existent footnote is emitted.
findings.suggested_fix: Reset/rebuild footnote_indexes whenever a new footnotes list is created, and ensure state.env['footnotes'] is set for the list actually used.

findings.explanation: footnote_indexes is only built when falsy and is never validated against the current footnotes list. If footnotes is replaced, cleared, or mutated outside this function (e.g. env reuse across documents), the cached indexes diverge from list positions, causing duplicate, missing, or inconsistent footnote indices.
findings.suggested_fix: Tie the cache to the identity/version of the footnotes list, rebuild it when footnotes changes, or derive the index from notes itself.

findings.explanation: Building indexes with a dict comprehension over enumerate(notes) makes a duplicated key in a pre-populated notes list map to its last occurrence, whereas its footnote position/label should correspond to the first occurrence, producing a wrong reference index.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the map keeping the first occurrence, e.g. only set indexes[note_key] if it is not already present.

findings.explanation: parse is called but never defined or imported in the file, so any path with removed=True or non-empty comments raises NameError.
findings.suggested_fix: import or define parse, e.g. from .parser import parse

findings.explanation: If a string is passed as comments, `if not comments` and `for comment in comments` iterate characters, producing wrong output like 'a; b; c' instead of error.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate isinstance(comments, list) (or tuple) and raise TypeError otherwise.

findings.explanation: Empty or whitespace-only entries are not filtered, so comments=['', 'a'] yields comment_text='; a' with leading separator and comments=[''] falls through incorrectly.
findings.suggested_fix: Filter falsy/blank comments, e.g. [c for c in comments if c and c.strip()] and check result.

findings.explanation: Newlines in comment or comment_prefix are not sanitized, so a comment containing '\n' breaks the single-line contract and injects extra lines.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject or replace '\r' and '\n' in comments and prefix, e.g. comment.replace('\n',' ').replace('\r',' ')

findings.explanation: Code and prefix are concatenated with no guaranteed separator, and default comment_prefix='' means output has no comment marker, producing e.g. 'code comment'.
findings.suggested_fix: Default comment_prefix to a real marker and normalize spacing, e.g. f"{code.rstrip()} {prefix} {comment_text}" stripped.

findings.explanation: original_string=None or non-str is not handled; parse(original_string) will crash instead of raising a clear error or using default.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate isinstance(original_string, str) and raise TypeError if not.

findings.explanation: parse is called on lines 9, 20, and 21 but is never defined or imported in the file, so every path except the empty-comments early return raises NameError at runtime.
findings.suggested_fix: Define parse or import it, e.g. add the missing 'from <module> import parse' at the top of the file.

findings.explanation: Empty or whitespace-only comment strings are not filtered: comments=[''] yields a bare trailing comment_prefix with no comment, and comments=['', 'x'] produces the malformed text '; x' with a leading separator.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip empty/blank entries while deduplicating, e.g. 'if comment and comment.strip() and comment not in unique_comments', and only append comment_prefix when comment_text is non-empty.

findings.explanation: Comment text (and comment_prefix) are interpolated verbatim, so a comment containing newline or carriage-return characters injects extra lines into the resulting line-based/config output and can corrupt or forge subsequent entries.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject or sanitize comments and prefix containing '\n' or '\r', e.g. raise ValueError or replace line breaks before joining.

findings.explanation: When comments is empty and removed is False the original_string is returned unchecked, so a caller passing original_string=None gets None back despite the declared '-> str' return type, while other paths crash inside parse(None).
findings.suggested_fix: Validate/coerce original_string up front, e.g. 'original_string = original_string or ""' before any branch so the function always returns a str.

findings.explanation: Condition is backwards: returns original unchanged when comments are present and falls through to merge logic when comments is empty/None.
findings.suggested_fix: if not comments: return original_string

findings.explanation: When comments is None the falsy check falls through and for comment in comments raises TypeError.
findings.suggested_fix: Handle None as empty, e.g. after fix `if not comments: return ...` so None returns early

findings.explanation: Removed path returns parse()[0] with the whitespace that preceded the stripped comment still attached.
findings.suggested_fix: return parse(original_string)[0].rstrip() or equivalent cleanup

findings.explanation: base.rstrip() on any line with an existing comment wipes out whitespace-only bases, destroying indentation of comment-only lines.
findings.suggested_fix: Only rstrip if base is not whitespace-only, e.g. `if base.strip(): base = base.rstrip()`

findings.explanation: When comment_text is empty still appends comment_prefix, and the f-string unconditionally adds a space, producing stray markers or double/trailing spaces.
findings.suggested_fix: if not comment_text: return base or original_string; else join prefix and text without unconditional extra space

findings.explanation: The guard is inverted: when comments is non-empty the function returns original_string unchanged, so supplied comments are never added.
findings.suggested_fix: Change to 'if not comments: return original_string'.

findings.explanation: comments is typed as list[str] | None, but with the current guard a None value falls through to 'for comment in comments', raising TypeError instead of returning original_string.
findings.suggested_fix: Return original_string when comments is None/empty: 'if not comments: return original_string' before iterating.

findings.explanation: An empty comments list falls through, parses and discards any existing comment, rstrips the base, and returns base+comment_prefix, thereby mutating a line that should be unchanged and leaving a dangling comment prefix.
findings.suggested_fix: Return original_string unchanged for empty/None comments before parsing or appending comment_prefix.

findings.explanation: If comments contains only empty strings, comment_text is empty yet the function still returns base+comment_prefix, adding a stray prefix with no comment text (and discarding any existing comment).
findings.suggested_fix: Filter out empty comment strings and, if comment_text is empty, return original_string (or at least base without comment_prefix).

findings.explanation: comment_text is computed but never used; return only appends comment_prefix so no comment is ever added.
findings.suggested_fix: return f"{base}{comment_prefix}{comment_text}"

findings.explanation: existing_comment parsed from original_string is discarded instead of preserved or merged, so adding comments silently drops the old comment.
findings.suggested_fix: merge existing_comment into unique_comments before joining, or preserve it if replacement is not intended

findings.explanation: parse is called but never defined or imported in this file, causing NameError on any call.
findings.suggested_fix: import parse from its module or define it in comments.py

findings.explanation: removed path returns parse()[0] with trailing whitespace left over from stripped comment, while add path rstrips it, leaving stray spaces.
findings.suggested_fix: return parse(original_string)[0].rstrip() or apply same whitespace handling as add path

findings.explanation: comment_text is computed but never used, so the returned string contains only base and comment_prefix and none of the requested comments are added.
findings.suggested_fix: return f"{base}{comment_prefix}{comment_text}"

findings.explanation: parse() strips any existing comment from original_string and it is never re-added or merged, so an existing comment distinct from the supplied comments is silently lost.
findings.suggested_fix: Append existing_comment to the result (deduplicated against unique_comments), e.g. include it in unique_comments before joining.

findings.explanation: base.rstrip() removes all leading/trailing whitespace when the base is indentation-only before a standalone comment (e.g. '    # c'), destroying the comment line's indentation instead of only removing the separator spacing before the comment.
findings.suggested_fix: Only rstrip when base.strip() is non-empty, e.g. 'base = base.rstrip() if base.strip() else base'.

findings.explanation: Match.group(-1) is invalid in Python; group indices start at 0, so this raises IndexError on every call.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace m.group(-1) with m.group(0) (or the intended capturing group, e.g. m.group(1))

findings.explanation: re.Match.group() does not support -1 as a last-group alias; calling m.group(-1) raises IndexError whenever state.cursor == 0, crashing on input beginning with a blank line.
findings.suggested_fix: Use m.group(0).count("\n") for the whole match (or the intended numbered capture group, e.g. m.group(1)).

findings.explanation: The else branch emits a blank_line token without the 'newlines' key present in the cursor==0 branch, so consumers expecting token["newlines"] will raise KeyError and the newline count for non-leading blank lines is lost.
findings.suggested_fix: Always include the count: state.append_token({"type": "blank_line", "newlines": m.group(0).count("\n")}) in both branches.

findings.explanation: Calls self.render_referrences with double-r, the correct spelling is render_references, so this raises AttributeError if the method is correctly named.
findings.suggested_fix: Change to self.render_references(state)

findings.explanation: Concatenates references directly onto `out` with no blank-line separator, so last block and first reference are glued together when `out` does not end with newlines.
findings.suggested_fix:
If refs non-empty and out non-empty: out += '

' + '

'.join(refs)

findings.explanation: Unconditionally appends "\n" even when there are no references, so empty refs still mutate `out` and empty document becomes "\n" unless strip_end strips newlines.
findings.suggested_fix: Only append when refs non-empty: refs=list(...); if refs: out += ...

findings.explanation: render_referrences is misspelled (extra 'r'); if the defined method is render_references, every call to __call__ raises AttributeError.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the call to self.render_references(state) to match the method definition.

findings.explanation: References are appended directly to out with no intervening blank line, so the first reference is glued onto the last rendered block whenever out does not already end with a blank line.
findings.suggested_fix:
refs = self.render_references(state); if refs: out += ('' if out.endswith('

') or not out else '

') + '

'.join(refs) + '
'

findings.explanation:
Expression "

".join(...) - "
" tries to subtract strings which raises TypeError on every call.
findings.suggested_fix:
Use string concatenation/slicing instead of -, e.g. out += "

" + "

".join(refs)

findings.explanation: Unconditionally appending joined references corrupts output when list is empty and misses required separator when out is non-empty.
findings.suggested_fix:
if refs: out = (out + "

" if out else "") + "

".join(refs)

findings.explanation: render_referrences is misspelled with double-r and will raise AttributeError if the API is render_references.
findings.suggested_fix: Call self.render_references(state)

findings.explanation: Direct tokens[i]["type"] raises KeyError if key missing, and blank_line without newlines stops loop leaving it to be rendered twice.
findings.suggested_fix: Use tokens[i].get("type") == "blank_line" and tokens[i].get("newlines", 0)

findings.explanation: The method is spelled render_referrences instead of render_references, so calling it will raise AttributeError unless an identically misspelled method exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the call to self.render_references(state).

findings.explanation: Subtracting a string from the string returned by join raises TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for -: 'str' and 'str', so every invocation reaching this line crashes.
findings.suggested_fix:
Use separate statements such as out += '
'; out += '

'.join(self.render_references(state)).

findings.explanation: Despite the line-break comment, no newline is added between the rendered body and the first reference, so references can be glued directly onto the preceding output.
findings.suggested_fix: Add out += '\n' before appending the joined references.

findings.explanation: strip_end removes trailing newlines and the result is returned without restoring the renderer's required single final newline, breaking the output contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Return strip_end(leading + out) + '\n'.

findings.explanation: Loop increments by 2 instead of 1, skipping tokens and possibly treating a non-leading blank_line as leading while dropping intermediate content.
Direct tokens[i]["type"] raises KeyError if a token lacks "type".
findings.suggested_fix: tokens[i].get("type") == "blank_line"

findings.explanation: References are concatenated directly to output without separator, so "para" + "[ref]" becomes "para[ref]" with missing blank lines.
findings.suggested_fix:
if refs: out = out.rstrip() + "

" + "

".join(refs) + "
"

findings.explanation: Unconditionally appends "\n" even when render_referrences returns empty, adding spurious newline.
findings.suggested_fix: only append references block when list is non-empty

findings.explanation: Block tokens store blank-line data under token['attrs']['newlines'], not token['newlines'], so the membership test is always false and leading blank lines are never preserved.
findings.suggested_fix: Use tokens[i].get('attrs', {}).get('newlines', 0) instead of checking/reading tokens[i]['newlines'].

findings.explanation: Advancing i by 2 skips the token after each leading blank_line; if it is content it is omitted from render_tokens, and if it is another blank_line its newlines are lost.
findings.suggested_fix: Change i += 2 to i += 1.

findings.explanation: For a document consisting only of blank lines, leading + out contains only newlines and the unconditional reference newline, so strip_end removes the very leading newlines this code tries to preserve and returns an empty string.
findings.suggested_fix: Handle the all-blank/no-content case explicitly, e.g. return leading.rstrip/stripped content only when there is rendered content, otherwise return the preserved newlines as intended.

findings.explanation: ord(start[-1]) runs before the length check, so empty slice raises IndexError and len 1-2 checks the wrong character ('<' or '/') instead of the tag-name start.
findings.suggested_fix: Check length first, then test rawdata[i+2], e.g. if len(start)<3: return -1; c=ord(start[2])

findings.explanation: A truncated buffer ending in '</' or '</x' is emitted as data instead of signaling incomplete input, so a tag split across feed() calls can never be recognized.
findings.suggested_fix: If i+3 > len(self.rawdata): return -1 to wait for more data

findings.explanation: Returning i+2 unconditionally can exceed len(rawdata) when only 1 char remains, violating the parser contract that the new offset is within the buffer.
findings.suggested_fix: Return min(i+2, len(self.rawdata)) or i+len(start)

findings.explanation: Emitting only '</' via handle_data splits one text node like '</>' into two handle_data calls instead of letting the main loop coalesce text.
findings.suggested_fix: Avoid direct handle_data here; treat as text and let goahead() coalesce or emit full bogus text at once

findings.explanation: ord(start[-1]) is evaluated before the len(start) < 3 guard, so an empty slice (i at or past end of rawdata) raises IndexError instead of being handled as data.
findings.suggested_fix: Check length first: if len(start) < 3: handle/return; only then read start[-1], e.g. 'if len(start) < 3 or not start[2].isalpha()' with short-circuit ordering.

findings.explanation: A trailing incomplete '</' (or '</' split across feed() chunks) has len(start) < 3 and is immediately emitted as data and consumed, so an end tag split across chunks (e.g. feed('</') then feed('div>')) is never recognised as an end tag.
findings.suggested_fix: When the buffer may be incomplete and EOF has not been reached, return -1 to wait for more data instead of consuming rawdata[i:i+2]; only treat it as data at true EOF.

findings.explanation: '</>' is classified as non-letter and emitted as literal data '</' followed by '>' as data, whereas the base parser/HTML spec drops the missing-end-tag-name token entirely by consuming all 3 characters.
findings.suggested_fix: Special-case rawdata[i:i+3] == '</>' and return i + 3 without calling handle_data.

findings.category: broken base-class contract for other non-letter end tags
findings.explanation: Inputs such as '</ div>', '</123>' or '</!...>' bypass super().parse_endtag(), losing its tolerant end-tag/bogus-comment handling; they are emitted as raw text and the remainder is re-parsed separately, producing different handle_data/handle_endtag/handle_comment events than the documented base behaviour (a sanitizer relying on those events can be desynchronised).
findings.suggested_fix: Only intercept the exact case that must be treated as character data, and delegate all other malformed end tags to super().parse_endtag(i).

findings.explanation: self.rawdata[i:i-2] is empty for i>=2 and rawdata[0:-2] for i==0 instead of the literal "</".
findings.suggested_fix: self.handle_data(self.rawdata[i:i+2])

findings.explanation: A -1 from super().parse_endtag() meaning '>' not found yet is conflated with bogus end-tag and consumed as data instead of returning -1 to wait for more data.
findings.suggested_fix: if not is_data: pos=super().parse_endtag(i); if pos==-1: return -1; return pos

findings.explanation: len(start)<3 e.g. buffer ends with "</" is forced to is_data and emitted instead of returning -1 for incremental feeding.
findings.suggested_fix: if len(start)<3: return -1 unless parser closed

findings.explanation: ord(start[-1]) raises IndexError if start is empty when i is at/past end of rawdata.
findings.suggested_fix: guard empty string before indexing, e.g. if not start: return -1

findings.explanation: ord(start[-1]) is evaluated before the len(start) < 3 check, so an empty slice (i at/past end of rawdata) raises IndexError instead of being treated as incomplete data.
findings.suggested_fix: Check length first, e.g. `if len(start) < 3: ...` before indexing, or use `c = ord(start[-1]) if start else -1`.

findings.explanation: self.rawdata[i:i - 2] is empty for i >= 2 and wraps to almost the whole buffer for i in (0, 1), so handle_data receives nothing or duplicated data instead of the intended '</'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `self.rawdata[i:i + 2]`.

findings.explanation: When super().parse_endtag(i) returns -1 it has already called handle_data on the entire remaining rawdata (EOF/no-match case); this code calls handle_data again and returns i + 2 instead of -1, duplicating data, discarding the rest of the tail, and violating goahead's expectation that -1 means incomplete input.
findings.suggested_fix: Only synthesize the data handling when is_data is true; otherwise propagate super's result: `return super().parse_endtag(i)` and for is_data handle '</' separately.

findings.explanation: len(start) < 3 means the tag may just be split across feed() calls (e.g. buffer ends with '</'); consuming it as data and returning i + 2 prevents it from ever being recognized as an end tag once the rest arrives.
findings.suggested_fix: When the buffer may be incomplete and EOF has not been signaled, return -1 to wait for more data instead of consuming '</' as data.

findings.explanation: The check requires an ASCII letter immediately after '</', but the tolerant end-tag regex in HTMLParser allows whitespace after '</' (e.g. '</ div>'), so valid end tags per the superclass contract are misclassified as data and never fire handle_endtag/clear_cdata_mode.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the superclass grammar (allow optional whitespace before the tag name) or only special-case constructs the superclass demonstrably rejects, such as '</>' and '</' followed by a non-name character with no whitespace.

findings.explanation: For input like '</ div>'-style or malformed tags where super fails to match, advancing only i + 2 leaves the remainder to be re-parsed piecemeal, whereas the original code treats the whole remainder as data at EOF; combined with the forced -1 this changes data chunking/content delivered to handlers including convert_charrefs/cdata paths.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the original -1 path untouched so the caller handles the full remainder exactly once under the existing charref/cdata logic.

findings.explanation: Slices i:i+2 so start is at most "</" and len(start)<3 is always true, so is_data is always True and super().parse_endtag() is never called.
findings.suggested_fix: Use start = self.rawdata[i:i+3] and test the char after "</"

findings.explanation: ord(start[-1]) raises IndexError if i is out of range or rawdata is exhausted and start is empty.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard empty start, e.g. if len(start)==0: return -1

findings.explanation: Truncated input like "</" at end of buffer is immediately emitted as data instead of returning -1 to wait for more feed() data, corrupting split feeds.
findings.suggested_fix: If not enough characters to decide (len<3), return -1 without calling handle_data

findings.explanation: A -1 from super().parse_endtag() meaning incomplete/invalid tag is conflated with bogus tag: it calls handle_data and returns i+2 instead of propagating -1, losing data and breaking goahead() contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Only handle_data/return i+2 when is_data is True; otherwise if pos==-1: return -1

findings.explanation: start contains only rawdata[i:i+2] ("</"), so len(start) < 3 is always true and start[-1] is always '/', never a letter. is_data is therefore always true, super().parse_endtag() is never called, and every valid end tag is emitted as data without invoking handle_endtag().
findings.suggested_fix: Inspect the third character, e.g. start = self.rawdata[i:i+3] and check start[2] for an ASCII letter.

findings.explanation: ord(start[-1]) is evaluated before the len(start) < 3 guard, so an empty slice at EOF raises IndexError instead of being treated as incomplete/data.
findings.suggested_fix: Check length first, e.g. if len(start) < 3: handle incomplete input; only index start after confirming it is non-empty.

findings.explanation: super().parse_endtag() returns -1 for incomplete or unterminated tags (e.g. '</di' awaiting 'v>' in a later feed()); this code conflates that with is_data, emits '</' as data and advances, corrupting chunked/incremental parsing and losing the end tag.
findings.suggested_fix: Propagate -1 from super() unchanged (return -1) so the caller buffers the partial tag; only emit data for definitively non-tag input.

findings.explanation: Even with the slice fixed, checking only the character immediately after '</' rejects whitespace-tolerant end tags such as '</ div>' that the stdlib endtagfind_tolerant regex (and thus super()) accepts, changing them into data.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the superclass grammar (allow optional whitespace before the tag name) or delegate to super() first and only fall back to data on definitive mismatch.

findings.explanation: When rawdata ends with a lone '<' or '</' at i, returning i + 2 advances past the end of the buffer and emits a two-character chunk that may not exist, instead of returning -1 so goahead() can await more data or apply EOF handling.
findings.suggested_fix: If fewer than 2 bytes remain, return -1; only return i + 2 after verifying rawdata[i:i+2] == '</'.

findings.explanation: zip(strict=...) requires Python 3.10+. On older supported versions this raises TypeError.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove strict=False or gate by sys.version_info, e.g. zip(...) without strict.

findings.explanation: Inserting combined 'x as y' strings into from_imports corrupts later lookups keyed by plain name.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep plain names in from_imports and expand aliases only at emit time; do not splice alias strings into from_imports.

findings.explanation: Lookup parsed.imports[...][from_import] assumes key exists; fails for '*' or spliced 'x as y' entries.
findings.suggested_fix: Use .get(from_import) with default and explicitly exclude '*' / alias strings.

findings.explanation: After combine_star, filtering to `in as_imports` keeps '*' if aliased and drops logic, causing duplicate star emission later.
findings.suggested_fix: Filter out '*' explicitly: [f for f in from_imports if f in as_imports and f != '*'] and clear star state.

findings.explanation: Star branch reuses `comments` without clearing, so same comments are emitted again on grouped statement; non-single-line star branch ignores `comments` entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass comments consistently to _with_star_comments and set comments=[] after emitting star.

findings.explanation: Leading-alias emission omits module-level `comments`, while force_single_line branch includes them, so comments are lost.
findings.suggested_fix: Include `comments` in straight_comments there and clear after first use like other branches.

findings.explanation: When from_import_section is empty comments are still attached to grouped call then unconditionally reset, silently dropping them.
findings.suggested_fix: Only reset comments when a statement was emitted; otherwise carry them to next iteration.

findings.explanation: Manual ';' vs comment_prefix join and extra `f" {comment}"` double-prefixes comments and produces wrong syntax.
findings.suggested_fix: Use with_comments for all comments instead of manual string concatenation.

findings.explanation: The grouped-section condition indexes parsed.imports with `from_import`, the leaked last value from earlier loops, instead of `from_imports[0]`. This can wrongly include/exclude an aliased name, drop its alias, lose comments on the resulting empty pass, or raise KeyError when the stale value is an expanded `x as y` string or another non-key.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `parsed.imports[section][import_key][module][from_imports[0]]` in the condition.

findings.explanation: When a name has both a nested comment and an alias and multi_line_output is NOQA, the guard at line 181 excludes NOQA, so the name is removed from from_imports and emitted as a plain single import; its `as` alias is never emitted and the binding semantics change.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the comment and defer aliased names to the leading-alias loop regardless of NOQA, or emit the alias(es) via _build_as_imports in this branch.

findings.explanation: The combine_star branch passes a copy of `comments` to _with_star_comments but never clears `comments`, so the same statement-level comments are reused for the following grouped/aliased output.
findings.suggested_fix: Clear after use, e.g. pass `comments` and set `comments = []` after appending the star line.

findings.explanation: Leading aliased imports are built without the statement-level `comments` (unlike the force_single_line path), and line 247 then unconditionally clears `comments` even when the grouped section is empty, so opening-line comments disappear when imports are alias-only or alias-first.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass/include `comments` for the first emitted aliased import and only clear `comments` once they have actually been consumed/emitted.

findings.explanation: The non-combine_star star import is appended via with_comments directly without wrap.line(parsed.line_separator, config), unlike the combine_star path, so wrapping/line-separator handling is ignored for long module names or comments.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap it the same way: `output.append(wrap.line(with_comments(...), parsed.line_separator, config))`.

findings.explanation: Uses subtraction on strings `import_start - from_import` which raises TypeError. Should concatenate.
findings.suggested_fix: Change to `import_start + from_import`.

findings.explanation: While condition indexes `parsed.imports...[from_import]` using stale loop variable instead of `from_imports[0]`, causing wrong grouping or KeyError.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `[from_import]` with `[from_imports[0]]`.

findings.explanation: Leading as-imports path passes only straight comments and drops `comments` from the opening from-line, unlike force_single_line and grouped paths.
findings.suggested_fix: Include `comments` in `straight_comments`, e.g. `[*comments, *straight.get(...)]` and clear after use.

findings.explanation: When combine_star is true the same `comments` list is used for the star line and then again for the grouped statement, duplicating them.
findings.suggested_fix: Clear `comments = []` after consuming them in the star block when `config.combine_star`.

findings.explanation: Appends nested comment with `(use_comments and ';') or config.comment_prefix`, emitting ';' instead of comment prefix when statement comments exist and mishandling prefix/spacing.
findings.suggested_fix: Always use `config.comment_prefix` and `with_comments` for the trailing comment instead of ';' concatenation.

findings.explanation: For non-last imports with nested comments `use_comments` is set to `[]`, discarding pending `comments` until the last element.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve/attach `comments` to first emitted line instead of dropping them.

findings.explanation: Strings do not support subtraction, so the force_single_line non-aliased path raises TypeError for every such import instead of building the line.
findings.suggested_fix: Use concatenation: import_start + from_import

findings.explanation: The second operand uses the stale loop variable `from_import` from the preceding nested-comment loop instead of the current head `from_imports[0]`, so whether an aliased name is included in the grouped statement is decided from a different import's straight-import flag, causing dropped or duplicated imports.
findings.suggested_fix: Use parsed.imports[section][import_key][module][from_imports[0]] in the condition.

findings.explanation: When multi_line_output is NOQA, the alias-deferral at line 181 is bypassed and a commented aliased name is removed from from_imports and emitted only as the straight `import_start + from_import`, so its `as` alias import is never emitted.
findings.suggested_fix: Also defer aliased names in NOQA mode (or emit their as-imports alongside the straight import) instead of emitting only the unaliased name.

findings.explanation: Condition accesses from_imports[1] without checking length, raising IndexError when one import remains, and checks the wrong element instead of index 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `while len(from_imports) > 1 and from_imports[0] in as_imports:` or `while from_imports and from_imports[0] in as_imports:`

findings.explanation: If from_imports[0] is in as_imports without combine_as straight import, from_import_section stays empty and from_imports makes no progress, looping forever. Triggered especially after combine_star filtering to alias-only list.
findings.suggested_fix: Ensure progress each outer iteration, e.g. handle alias-only remainder via _build_as_imports or break when from_import_section empty and from_imports unchanged.

findings.explanation: combine_star filtering keeps only aliased names even when combine_as_imports is false, so non-aliased names are dropped and remaining alias-only list stalls in the grouped logic.
findings.suggested_fix: Only filter when combining as-imports applies, or handle alias-only list in non-combine_as path.

findings.explanation: Star line uses `comments` when combine_star is true but never clears it, so same comments are reused for the next grouped/single-line statement.
findings.suggested_fix: After emitting star with combined comments set `comments = []` when config.combine_star.

findings.explanation: Second inline comment is joined with `';'` without comment_prefix, producing `; comment` instead of `; # comment`, and `use_comments and ';'` misuses list truthiness.
findings.suggested_fix: Use e.g. `f"; {config.comment_prefix}{comment_text}"` or preserve prefix explicitly.

findings.explanation: zip(strict=False) requires Python 3.10+ and crashes on older versions.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove `strict=False` or guard by Python version; lengths are already equal.

findings.explanation: The leading-alias loop tests from_imports[1] instead of from_imports[0]: it raises IndexError when one import remains, processes a non-aliased first import as aliased (KeyError/wrong output) when the second is aliased, and skips an aliased first import when the second is not.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `while from_imports and from_imports[0] in as_imports:`

findings.explanation: The grouped-section condition reads parsed.imports[...][module][from_import] using the stale loop variable `from_import` instead of the candidate `from_imports[0]`, so combine_as decisions are based on the wrong name (and can KeyError/NameError or consume aliased imports incorrectly).
findings.suggested_fix: Use `parsed.imports[section][import_key][module][from_imports[0]]`

findings.explanation: The leading-alias path omits the pending opening-line `comments` from straight_comments (unlike the force_single_line path), so those comments are deferred to a later grouped statement or cleared at line 247 instead of appearing with the aliased import that consumed the opening line.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass `straight_comments=[*comments, *parsed.categorized_comments['straight'].get(f"{module}.{from_import}", [])]` and clear `comments` after first use

findings.explanation: When a nested comment exists on an aliased name and multi_line_output is NOQA, the restore-and-defer guard is bypassed, the name is removed and emitted as a plain single import, and its entries in as_imports are never emitted, silently losing the `as` imports.
findings.suggested_fix: Defer aliased names regardless of wrap mode (remove the NOQA exception) or emit _build_as_imports for them in this branch

findings.explanation: renderer and plugins can be unhashable (e.g. plugins is commonly a list, renderer can be an instance), so using (escape, renderer, plugins) as a dict key raises TypeError.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize key e.g. plugins_key = None if plugins is None else tuple(plugins) and handle unhashable renderer via id() or skip caching.

findings.explanation: Every distinct key is cached forever with no eviction, so many distinct renderers/plugins cause memory exhaustion.
findings.suggested_fix: Bound the cache with functools.lru_cache(maxsize=...) or only cache the default (escape, renderer) cases.

findings.explanation: Cached Markdown instance is reused across calls and threads; if the parser holds per-parse state it can leak state or race.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard reuse with a lock, copy/reset parser per call, or cache a factory instead of an instance.

findings.explanation: plugins is documented/typed as an Iterable and callers commonly pass a list (e.g. plugins=['table']); using it directly in a dict key raises TypeError: unhashable type: 'list', breaking the normal API.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize before keying: plugins_key = tuple(plugins) if plugins is not None else None, and pass that tuple to create_markdown.

findings.explanation: renderer can be a custom renderer instance; instances of classes defining __eq__ without __hash__ (or mutable-hash objects) are unhashable or change hash, so the lookup can crash or never hit/corrupt cache entries.
findings.suggested_fix: Only cache for known hashable renderer values (str/None), or key custom renderers by id(renderer) and handle unhashable types by bypassing the cache.

findings.explanation: If plugins is a generator/iterator it is keyed by identity, so every call creates a new useless cache entry and create_markdown consumes it; a reused exhausted iterator can also incorrectly hit the earlier entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Materialize plugins once into a tuple before computing the key and creating the parser.

findings.explanation: Entries are added to __cached_parsers forever with no size limit or eviction, and keys/parsers hold strong references to renderer and plugin objects, preventing their garbage collection and allowing unbounded memory growth from varied arguments.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a bounded cache (e.g. functools.lru_cache with maxsize, or a size-limited dict) and do not retain arbitrary user objects longer than needed.

findings.explanation: Previously each call built a fresh Markdown/renderer; now one parser (and for 'html' its renderer) is shared across all threads/calls, so any state mutated by the renderer or plugins during a parse can leak or race between concurrent parses.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not cache/share parser instances unless thread-safety is guaranteed; cache only immutable configuration, use a lock/per-thread parsers, or create a fresh parser per call.

findings.explanation: Condition uses `or` instead of `and`, so a non-cacheable custom renderer with string/empty plugins, or a cacheable renderer with callable plugin objects, still takes the cached path and raises TypeError on unhashable args or pollutes cache.
findings.suggested_fix: Change `or` to `and`: `if (renderer is None or renderer in ('html','ast')) and all(...)`

findings.explanation: If `plugins` is a single string like 'footnotes', `tuple(plugins)` splits it into characters producing wrong plugins.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `if isinstance(plugins, str): plugin_refs = (plugins,)` before tupling.

findings.explanation: Reusing the same cached `md` object across calls leaks parser state between documents and is not thread-safe.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not cache the Markdown instance; cache the configuration and call `create_markdown(...)` per invocation or return a copy.

findings.explanation: The condition uses OR, so a custom non-string renderer is routed to _cached_markdown whenever plugins are absent or all strings, because all() is true for an empty tuple and for string plugins. The cached path expects only None/'html'/'ast' renderer refs and may reject, misinterpret, or fail to hash a custom renderer object/class.
findings.suggested_fix: Require both sides: if (renderer is None or renderer == 'html' or renderer == 'ast') and all(isinstance(p, str) for p in plugin_refs):

findings.explanation: With the default/'html'/'ast'/None renderer, non-string plugin objects, classes, or callables are still routed to _cached_markdown because the first operand is true. The cached path expects string plugin refs and may fail lookup or raise TypeError if a plugin is unhashable, instead of using create_markdown which accepts live plugin objects.
findings.suggested_fix: Require both sides: if (renderer is None or renderer == 'html' or renderer == 'ast') and all(isinstance(p, str) for p in plugin_refs):

findings.explanation: lru_cache caches and reuses the same mutable Markdown instance across calls, so parser state leaks between calls and concurrent use races.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not cache the Markdown instance; cache the configuration or return a copy e.g. copy.deepcopy(_cached_markdown(...)) or create a new instance per call.

findings.explanation: If plugins is a single string, tuple(plugins) splits it into characters, e.g. 'table' becomes ('t','a','b','l','e'), producing wrong results.
findings.suggested_fix: Check isinstance(plugins, str) first: plugin_refs = (plugins,) if isinstance(plugins, str) else tuple(plugins) ...

findings.explanation: The change shares one Markdown/parser/renderer instance across all calls with the same arguments, whereas previously each call created a fresh instance. Mistune parser/renderer/plugin state is not guaranteed thread-safe or reentrant, so concurrent or nested markdown() calls can corrupt each other's parse state and produce wrong output.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not share Markdown instances across threads/reentrant calls; use a thread-local cache, a per-call instance, or serialize access to the cached instance with a lock.

findings.explanation: If plugins is passed as a single plugin name string, tuple(plugins) splits it into individual characters; the all-str check then routes it to the cached path and create_markdown will look up one-character plugin names instead of the intended plugin.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize a string plugin first, e.g. plugin_refs = (plugins,) if isinstance(plugins, str) else tuple(plugins) if plugins is not None else ().

findings.explanation: Builtin detection uses == against strings, so a non-string renderer object whose __eq__ matches "html"/"ast" can be routed into _cached_markdown; if that object is unhashable (common when __eq__ is defined) lru_cache raises TypeError instead of letting create_markdown handle/reject it as before.
findings.suggested_fix: Route to the cache only for actual builtin strings/None, e.g. check renderer is None or (isinstance(renderer, str) and renderer in ("html", "ast")).

findings.explanation: lru_cache caches and reuses the same mutable Markdown instance across calls, so parser state leaks between calls and concurrent md(text) calls race/corrupt each other.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not cache Markdown instances; cache config or return a copy per call, e.g. copy.deepcopy(_cached_markdown(...)) or create fresh via create_markdown each call.

findings.explanation: If plugins is a single string it is Iterable, so tuple(plugins) splits it into characters producing wrong plugins.
findings.suggested_fix: if isinstance(plugins, str): plugin_refs = (plugins,) elif plugins is not None: plugin_refs = tuple(plugins) else: plugin_refs = ()

findings.explanation: Condition uses isinstance(renderer, str) or renderer in ("html","ast"), so any string renderer is treated as builtin and sent to _cached_markdown typed for builtins only.
findings.suggested_fix: Change to isinstance(renderer, str) and renderer in ("html", "ast") (plus None handling) so only builtins use cached path.

findings.explanation: tuple(plugins) assumes plugins is iterable and crashes with TypeError if a single non-iterable plugin object/callable is passed.
findings.suggested_fix: Detect non-iterable / single plugin and wrap it, e.g. try tuple or handle callable/non-iterable as single entry.

findings.explanation: The same Markdown instance is returned from the cache and reused for every call with the same arguments, whereas previously each call got a fresh parser/renderer. A Markdown parser/renderer is mutable during parsing, so concurrent calls or reentrant calls from a plugin/renderer with the same cache key can corrupt each other's state and produce wrong output or crashes.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not cache and share Markdown instances across calls unless thread-safety/reentrancy is guaranteed; cache only immutable configuration and construct a new Markdown per markdown() call, or guard reuse with locking and forbid reentry.

findings.explanation: plugins=None is normalized to an empty tuple and that empty tuple is passed to create_markdown on both the cached and non-cached paths. This breaks the contract if create_markdown treats plugins=None as 'use the default plugin set', silently disabling default plugins for the common markdown(text) call.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve None when delegating: use a distinct cache-key sentinel for None and call create_markdown(..., plugins=None) in that case instead of plugins=().

findings.explanation: isinstance(renderer, str) makes the renderer in ("html", "ast") test dead code and sends every string renderer, including invalid or non-builtin names, into _cached_markdown despite its _BuiltinRendererRef contract. The cache eligibility check therefore does not actually restrict caching to the builtin renderers it claims to support.
findings.suggested_fix: Cache only for known builtin renderers: if renderer is None or renderer in ("html", "ast"): (with an exact type/value check), otherwise delegate uncached.

findings.category: unsafe equality check on custom renderer
findings.explanation: For a non-string renderer, renderer in ("html", "ast") invokes that object's __eq__ against strings before the call falls through to the uncached path. Custom renderer objects/callables with unusual or raising __eq__ implementations (or array-like equality results) can therefore crash or misbehave even though they are valid uncached renderers.
findings.suggested_fix: Check renderer is None or (type(renderer) is str and renderer in ("html", "ast")) so custom renderer objects never undergo string equality tests for cache eligibility.

findings.category: stale cache after plugin registry changes
findings.explanation: String plugin names are resolved to plugin callables when the Markdown instance is built, but the cache key only stores the names. If the builtin plugin registry is extended or a plugin name is rebound at runtime, subsequent markdown() calls keep using the stale cached parser instead of resolving the new plugin.
findings.suggested_fix: Include a registry version/generation in the cache key, provide cache invalidation when plugins are registered, or do not cache parsers built from mutable plugin registries.

findings.explanation: def run is indented inside unique so it is a nested local function, not a method; the class loses its treeprocessor and module has IndentationError.
findings.suggested_fix: Dedent def run to module/class level: `def run...` or `    def run...` inside class, not inside unique.

findings.explanation: Pre-existing ids are never passed through unique(), so duplicate or empty id="" attributes in source remain duplicated and invalid.
findings.suggested_fix: Always normalize: `el.attrib['id'] = unique(el.attrib.get('id') or slug..., used_ids)` or if present check duplicates and replace if duplicate/empty.

findings.explanation: Unescaping toc token id with unescape() diverges from actual element id attribute, breaking TOC links and injecting raw chars like quotes.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `'id': el.attrib["id"]` without unescape to keep token and DOM identical.

findings.explanation: Wrapping data-toc-label name with escape_cdata() double-escapes when TOC is later serialized.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `name = strip_tags(data_toc_label)` without escape_cdata, escaping only at serialization.

findings.explanation: int(el.tag[-1]) assumes h1-h6 tags and crashes with ValueError for custom header_rgx matches.
findings.suggested_fix: Parse level via regex group from header_rgx or guard with try/except.

findings.explanation: `run` is indented inside `unique` after its `return`, so it is only a nested function definition that is never executed and is not a method of the treeprocessor class; the TOC processing will never run as a processor method.
findings.suggested_fix: Dedent `run` into the treeprocessor class (and restore the class definition/signature) so it is defined as `TocTreeprocessor.run`.

findings.explanation: The token stores `unescape(el.attrib["id"])`, but the element, anchors and permalinks keep the original attribute value. For ids containing entity-like text (e.g. `a&b` / `<`) the TOC href/id no longer matches the heading id and can emit broken or unsafe markup.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the exact attribute value: `'id': el.attrib["id"]` (do not HTML-unescape an already-parsed XML attribute).

findings.explanation: `el.attrib['data-toc-label']` is already entity-decoded by the XML parser; calling `unescape` again turns literal text such as `&lt;` into `<`, so `strip_tags` can delete intended text or treat user text as markup, while `escape_cdata(strip_tags(...))` then re-escapes surviving text and can double-encode the displayed label.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not unescape the parsed attribute again; sanitize once, e.g. `data_toc_label = run_postprocessors(el.attrib['data-toc-label'], self.md)` and set `name` from the sanitized text without an extra blanket escape.

findings.explanation: The loop iterates lazily over `doc.iter()` while `remove_fnrefs(el)`, `add_anchor` and `add_permalink` can remove/append children of elements in that same tree. Mutating the tree during `iter()` can cause newly added nodes to be visited and, depending on the mutation, siblings/headers to be skipped.
findings.suggested_fix: Materialize the header list first (e.g. `headers = [el for el in doc.iter() if ...]`) and operate on a copy in `remove_fnrefs`, then mutate anchors/permalinks after collecting headers.

findings.explanation: Every registered postprocessor is run unconditionally on the serialized TOC fragment. Stateful/non-idempotent postprocessors (e.g. raw-HTML stash or reference handling) are designed to run once on the full document; running them here can consume/alter shared state, transform TOC markup unexpectedly, or return `None` and break the next iteration / leave `md.toc` as `None`.
findings.suggested_fix: Only run the postprocessors that are safe/required for the TOC fragment, guard against `None` returns, or serialize the TOC after document postprocessing instead of re-running the whole registry on a fragment.

findings.explanation: count += 0 leaves count at 0 for a base without suffix, so first duplicate becomes base_0 instead of base_1 and breaks the documented '_1','_2' contract.
findings.suggested_fix: change to count += 1 before the while loop

findings.explanation: def run is indented inside unique() after return id, so it is never defined/executed and the TOC processor never runs.
findings.suggested_fix: dedent def run to class/top level so it is a reachable method

findings.explanation: iterating self.md.postprocessors yields keys/names, not processors, so pp.run crashes; Markdown uses a registry.
findings.suggested_fix: use self.md.postprocessors.run(toc) or iterate .values()

findings.explanation: Pre-existing duplicate header ids are never passed through unique(), leaving duplicate id attributes in output and ambiguous TOC links.
findings.suggested_fix: call unique() on existing ids without overwriting when already unique, or track and deduplicate

findings.explanation: int(el.tag[-1]) assumes single-digit h-tag and will ValueError or mis-level on namespaced/unexpected tags matched by header_rgx.
findings.suggested_fix: parse level from regex group instead of tag[-1]

findings.explanation: The suffix counter is not incremented before searching for a free id, so a duplicated plain id such as 'foo' (count=0) returns 'foo_0' instead of the documented 'foo_1', and an empty id returns '_0' instead of '_1'.
findings.suggested_fix: Change `count += 0` to `count += 1` so the search starts at the first appended suffix (after applying the counters skip, this also starts correctly at known+1).

findings.explanation: def run is indented inside def unique after return id, so it is never defined as a method and never runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Dedent def run to class level (0 or class indent) so it is a normal method.

findings.explanation: Condition uses or instead of and, so every element with string tag is treated as header and non-string tags evaluate header_rgx.match on non-string causing TypeError.
findings.suggested_fix: if isinstance(el.tag, str) and self.header_rgx.match(el.tag):

findings.explanation: Pre-existing duplicate ids are never uniquified; used_ids is a set so duplicates collapse and both elements keep the same id.
findings.suggested_fix: Always normalize header id via unique(), e.g. if pre-existing id different after unique() assign it.

findings.explanation: Once non-headers are processed, int(el.tag[-1]) raises ValueError and el.attrib["id"] raises KeyError for elements without ids.
findings.suggested_fix: Only process headers (fix line 43) and guard tag parsing / use el.attrib.get("id").

findings.explanation: The condition uses `or`, so every element with a string tag is treated as a header, and for non-string tags (comments/PIs) `header_rgx.match(el.tag)` raises TypeError. Non-headers then get ids/anchors and `int(el.tag[-1])` at line 60 can raise ValueError, corrupting the document or crashing.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `if isinstance(el.tag, str) and self.header_rgx.match(el.tag):` so only actual header elements are processed.

findings.explanation: parse_title can return None or empty and is used directly in os.path.join/realpath, causing TypeError or including the source directory itself.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate relpath is a non-empty str and return block_error otherwise.

findings.explanation: os.path.commonpath raises ValueError on different drives on Windows or empty paths, crashing the parse instead of returning block_error.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap commonpath check in try/except ValueError and return block_error.

findings.explanation: User-supplied encoding is passed directly to bytes.decode, so unknown encoding raises LookupError and bad bytes raise UnicodeDecodeError.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate encoding with codecs.lookup and catch LookupError/UnicodeDecodeError, return block_error.

findings.explanation: isfile to open is TOCTOU and open/read can raise OSError, PermissionError, FileNotFoundError which are unhandled and crash parsing.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap open/read in try/except OSError and return block_error.

findings.explanation: Entire file is read with no size limit, allowing memory exhaustion with a large included file.
findings.suggested_fix: Enforce max include size, check st_size and limit f.read().

findings.explanation: Extension comparison is case-sensitive so .MD, .Markdown, .HTML fall through to wrong token type.
findings.suggested_fix: Use os.path.splitext(dest)[1].lower() for comparison.

findings.explanation: Any non-md/html extension including binary is decoded as text, causing UnicodeDecodeError or mojibake in raw.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject binary/unknown extensions or handle errors, don't return decoded binary as include raw.

findings.explanation: Included .html content is emitted as raw block_html with no sanitization, allowing script injection if included file is attacker-controlled.
findings.suggested_fix: Sanitize HTML or document trust requirement / escape by default.

findings.explanation: Absolute filesystem dest realpath is exposed in attrs filepath, leaking server layout to output.
findings.suggested_fix: Store relpath or redacted path instead of absolute dest.

findings.explanation: Cycle stack lives in state.env but markdown include parses in new_state from child_state; if env is copied the stack is not shared and circular includes recurse infinitely with no depth limit.
findings.suggested_fix: Propagate shared stack explicitly to child state and enforce max include depth.

findings.explanation: Opening/reading and decoding the file can raise OSError/PermissionError, UnicodeDecodeError, or LookupError for an invalid user-supplied encoding; none are converted to block_error, so a bad included file or encoding crashes the whole parse.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap read/decode in try/except (OSError, UnicodeError, LookupError) and return {'type': 'block_error', 'raw': '...'}.

findings.explanation: If parse_title returns None or an empty/invalid title, os.path.join/realpath raises TypeError/ValueError (e.g. embedded NUL) instead of producing a block_error.
findings.suggested_fix: Check `if not relpath` (and reject NUL) before joining and return a block_error for a missing include path.

findings.explanation: Extension matching is case-sensitive, so files like PAGE.MD or PAGE.HTML are not parsed/treated as HTML and fall through to the generic raw 'include' token, producing wrong output.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `ext = os.path.splitext(dest)[1].lower()` before comparing.

findings.explanation: Containment, self-include and circular-include checks use exact string comparison of realpath results; on case-insensitive filesystems (Windows/macOS) the same file spelled with different case compares unequal, bypassing self/circular detection and causing unbounded recursive inclusion (RecursionError).
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize keys with os.path.normcase(os.path.realpath(...)) for source_file, dest, containment and stack membership.

findings.explanation: The isfile check and the later open are separate operations; the path (or a symlink component) can be swapped in between, so a directory, device, or outside file can be opened despite the earlier checks.
findings.suggested_fix: Open once and validate with os.fstat (regular file) on the descriptor, re-checking the opened path if strict containment is required.

findings.explanation: The entire included file is read into memory with no size limit, so including a very large file inside the source directory exhausts memory/CPU during parsing.
findings.suggested_fix: Stat/fstat the file and enforce a maximum include size, reading at most limit+1 bytes and returning block_error when exceeded.

findings.explanation: Any readable file under the source directory (e.g. .env, .git/config, private keys with an unknown extension) is returned verbatim as raw content/HTML, so an include directive can leak secrets into rendered output; there is no denylist for hidden/sensitive files.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject hidden files/directories and sensitive names/extensions, or restrict includes to an allowlist of extensions.

findings.explanation: Uses `-` instead of `+` for string concatenation, raising TypeError when a circular include is detected.
findings.suggested_fix: "Could not include circular reference: " + relpath

findings.explanation: Early returns pop `source_added` then `finally` pops again unconditionally, corrupting `__include_stack__` and breaking later cycle detection.
findings.suggested_fix: Don't pop before return; let single `finally` pop dest if appended and source if added via flags.

findings.explanation: os.path.commonpath raises ValueError on empty paths or different drives on Windows, crashing parse instead of returning block_error.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap in try/except ValueError and return block_error.

findings.explanation: Return value of parse_title is not validated; None, empty, or non-str causes TypeError in os.path.join/realpath/isabs.
findings.suggested_fix: Check if not relpath or not isinstance(relpath,str): return block_error

findings.explanation: User-supplied encoding is never validated; invalid name raises LookupError and bad bytes raise UnicodeDecodeError, crashing the parser.
findings.suggested_fix: try: codecs.lookup(encoding) and try/except UnicodeDecodeError/LookupError around decode and return block_error

findings.explanation: isfile check then open is racy and OSError (missing, permission, symlink swap, directory) is unhandled, crashing parse.
findings.suggested_fix: try/except OSError around open/read and return block_error

findings.explanation: Extension comparison is case-sensitive so .MD/.Markdown/.HTML files are misclassified as generic include instead of markdown/html.
findings.suggested_fix: ext = os.path.splitext(dest)[1].lower()

findings.explanation: Self and circular checks use realpath equality without normcase, bypassable by case variation on case-insensitive filesystems.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare os.path.normcase(realpath) values.

findings.explanation: Exposes absolute server filesystem path in attrs['filepath'].
findings.suggested_fix: Store relative path or omit; don't leak dest.

findings.explanation: File is read unbounded with no size or include-depth limit, allowing memory exhaustion and deep recursive includes.
findings.suggested_fix: Enforce max_bytes and max include depth/recursion limit.

findings.explanation: String subtraction '"..." - relpath' raises TypeError instead of returning the circular-reference block_error, crashing parsing whenever a cycle is detected.
findings.suggested_fix: Change '-' to '+': "Could not include circular reference: " + relpath

findings.explanation: If parse_title returns None or an empty title, os.path.join/isabs raises TypeError or dest silently becomes source_dir, instead of returning a block_error.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard 'if not relpath: return {"type": "block_error", "raw": "Missing include path"}' before joining paths.

findings.explanation: os.path.isabs(relpath) rejects every absolute path, even one that resolves inside source_dir, contradicting the 'outside source dir' error and contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the isabs check and rely only on the realpath commonpath containment check (which also handles absolute paths on another drive if guarded).

findings.explanation: open/read can raise OSError (permission, race after isfile check) and decode can raise UnicodeDecodeError or LookupError for a user-supplied bogus encoding; none are converted to block_error, so a bad include crashes the whole parse.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap open/decode in try/except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, LookupError) returning a block_error, and validate encoding with codecs.lookup first.

findings.explanation: Extensions are compared case-sensitively, so files like PAGE.MD or PAGE.HTML are misclassified as plain 'include' instead of being parsed as markdown/HTML, producing wrong output (common on case-insensitive filesystems).
findings.suggested_fix: Use ext = os.path.splitext(dest)[1].lower() before the set comparisons.

findings.explanation: The containment check is done on realpath before open, but open(dest) re-resolves the path; swapping dest for a symlink to outside source_dir between check and open escapes the sandbox.
findings.suggested_fix: Open the file then verify os.path.realpath('/proc/self/fd/%d' % f.fileno()) (or re-realpath and compare while holding the fd / use dir_fd with O_NOFOLLOW) is still within source_dir before reading.

findings.explanation: f.read() loads the entire included file into memory with no size limit, so including a huge file causes memory exhaustion/DoS.
findings.suggested_fix: Read with a size cap (e.g. read(limit+1) and return block_error if exceeded).

findings.explanation: Self-inclusion and cycle detection compare only realpath strings, so a hard link (different path, same inode) to the source file is not detected as self-inclusion at this level and its content gets included once before cycle logic catches it.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare os.path.samestat/os.stat st_dev+st_ino of dest and source_file in addition to path equality.

findings.explanation: parse_title can return None or empty, then os.path.join/os.path.isabs raise TypeError or resolve to a directory.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate relpath is non-empty string and return block_error otherwise.

findings.explanation: os.path.commonpath raises ValueError on different drives or invalid paths, crashing parse instead of returning block_error.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap commonpath check in try/except ValueError and treat as outside-dir error.

findings.explanation: Condition is inverted: returns 'Could not find file' when file exists and proceeds to open when it does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Change to `if not os.path.isfile(dest):`

findings.explanation: Directories, permissions, missing files, null bytes cause open() to raise IsADirectoryError, FileNotFoundError, PermissionError, ValueError which is uncaught.
findings.suggested_fix: Check isfile/isdir and wrap open in try/except OSError/ValueError returning block_error.

findings.explanation: User-controlled encoding can be unknown or wrong, raising LookupError, UnicodeDecodeError, TypeError and crashing.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate encoding with codecs.lookup and wrap decode in try/except returning block_error.

findings.explanation: Extension check is case-sensitive so .MD, .HTML includes fall through to generic include.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `os.path.splitext(dest)[1].lower()`

findings.explanation: Storing absolute realpath dest in attrs['filepath'] leaks server filesystem layout to output.
findings.suggested_fix: Store relpath or omit filepath, and pop user-supplied encoding/filepath handling.

findings.explanation: File is read unbounded into memory with no size limit, allowing huge file to cause DoS.
findings.suggested_fix: Enforce max include size with stat check and limited read.
